segments: 75. The Eighth Period.
The Emperors of the Romans.
And in his eighth year,
Zāmāsp (Zāmāfas,
Zāmashp?) rebelled against his brother Kawād and reigned two years.
And Kawād fled, gathered an army, and came against his brother;
and he defeated him and killed him,
and reigned after that thirty years.
At this time, Nicopolis was overturned,
and buried all its inhabitants,
except for the bishop and two attendants of his cell.
And a comet {OCR?} was seen for many days.
And again locusts came and caused destruction,
and there was a great famine in Mesopotamia.
And again a great fire was seen in the northern region,
which was flashing brightly all night.
And shortly after, the Huns who were in the northwest went out against the Persians for a reason such as this:
For in the days of Zeno, the Huns sent to Peroz, king of the Persians, and said to him
that the tribute he gave them was not sufficient for them,
and that the Romans gave double.
"Therefore, either give as the Romans do,
or prepare for war."
Now that Peroz deceived them and said that he would give it,
and upon this condition the Huns turned back.
Peroz, however, having grown bold, killed {OCR?} the Huns who were left to receive the tribute,
and pursued {OCR?} those who had gone.
Then a certain Greek merchant from Apamea who was with the Huns encouraged them,
and advised that they should offer incense at the place where the oath had been made,
and God would overthrow the Persians who had lied.
And when they did so,
they met the Persians,
and killed Peroz,
and plundered Persia,
and returned to their country.
And because of this, when Kawād reigned,
he harbored resentment against the Romans;
and they gathered armies and went out against the territories of the Romans.
And he captured Theodosiopolis of Armenia, which is Erzurum,
and treated its inhabitants with mercy.
He took Constantine, the governor there, captive.
And in Tishrin he encamped against Amid with great fury.
And when winter overtook them,
the Persians suffered,
because their garments were loose {OCR?},
and their bows became slack from the dampness of the air,
and the heads of their battering rams did not harm the wall,
because the defenders inside tied logs of raft-timber {OCR?} with chains,
